[Series](index.qmd) · **Foundations** · [Violin](violin.qmd) · [Clarinet](clarinet.qmd) · [Kalimba](kalimba.qmd) · [Harmonica](harmonica.qmd) · [Piano](piano.qmd) · [Drum](drum.qmd)

Build a string out of beads, apply Newton's law to one bead, and let the beads crowd together. The wave equation falls out, and so does the reason a string's overtones are whole numbers.

## One bead, two pulls

1. Put $N$ beads of mass $m$ on a massless thread with tension $T$, spaced $h$ apart, with both ends tied down. Let $u_j$ be the height of bead $j$, and set $u_0 = u_{N+1} = 0$ for the tied ends.
2. The thread on the right pulls bead $j$ along itself with force $T$. For small slopes its vertical part is $T\sin\theta \approx T\tan\theta = T(u_{j+1}-u_j)/h$. The thread on the left contributes $T(u_{j-1}-u_j)/h$.
3. Newton's second law for bead $j$ is therefore
$$
m\,\ddot u_j = \frac{T}{h}\left(u_{j+1} - 2u_j + u_{j-1}\right).
$$

The right side is a second difference: it measures how far bead $j$ sits below the average of its neighbors. Drag a bead and watch the arrows.

```{=html}
<div class="ins">
<div class="panel">
    <canvas id="beads" style="height:230px" aria-label="Beads on a string; drag a bead vertically"></canvas>
    <div class="slider"><label for="nb">Beads N</label><input type="range" id="nb" min="1" max="30" step="1" value="5"><output id="nbo">5</output></div>
    <div class="controls"><button class="primary" id="release">Release</button><button id="reset">Reset to a pluck</button><button id="hear">Hear these beads</button></div>
    <p class="cap">Arrows show the net vertical force on each bead, rescaled to stay visible as N grows. Drag any bead, then release.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Crowd the beads together

4. Fix the total length $L = (N+1)h$ and the mass per length $\mu = m/h$. Dividing the bead equation by $m = \mu h$ gives
$$
\ddot u_j = \frac{T}{\mu}\cdot\frac{u_{j+1} - 2u_j + u_{j-1}}{h^2}.
$$
5. As $h \to 0$ the second difference divided by $h^2$ tends to $u_{xx}$, by Taylor's theorem. With $c^2 = T/\mu$ this is the wave equation.

::: {.result}
**The string's operator.**
$$
u_{tt} = -\mathcal{L}u, \qquad \mathcal{L} = -c^2\partial_x^2, \qquad u(0) = u(L) = 0 .
$$
:::

The bead chain also has an exact spectrum. Its frequencies are $\omega_n = 2\sqrt{T/mh}\,\sin\big(n\pi/2(N+1)\big)$ for $n = 1,\dots,N$. Slide $N$ up: for small $n$ the sine is nearly linear, and the stems land on the integer grid.

```{=html}
<div class="ins">
<div class="panel">
    <h3>Spectrum of the bead chain</h3>
    <svg class="spec" id="chainSpec" viewBox="0 0 320 120" aria-label="Frequencies of the bead chain relative to the lowest one"></svg>
    <div class="readout" id="chainRead"></div>
    <p class="cap">Gray lines are whole-number multiples of the lowest frequency. Stem height is how strongly the current shape excites each mode.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {.qa}
<details><summary><span class="label">Reader question</span>$u'' + k^2 u = 0$ has a single $k$. Where does an infinite list of frequencies come from?</summary>

In that equation $k$ was fixed in advance. The eigenvalue problem asks the reverse: for which $k$ does $u'' + k^2u = 0$ have a nonzero solution that also satisfies $u(0) = u(L) = 0$? The first condition leaves $u = \sin kx$, and the second needs $\sin kL = 0$, so $k = \pi/L, 2\pi/L, 3\pi/L, \dots$ Each $k$ gives one shape; the boundary conditions admit infinitely many of them. The count matches the degrees of freedom: the $N$ beads above have exactly $N$ frequencies, the continuous string has infinitely many, and a string with no ends at all would accept every $k$, a continuous spectrum.

</details>
:::

::: {.qa}
<details><summary><span class="label">Reader question</span>How is the shape $X_n(x)$ related to the factor $\cos(\omega_n t)$?</summary>

Both come from separating variables. Substituting $u = X(x)\,T(t)$ into $u_{tt} = c^2 u_{xx}$ gives $T''/T = c^2X''/X$. The left side depends only on $t$ and the right only on $x$, so both equal one constant, $-\omega^2$. That splits the equation in two: $T'' = -\omega^2 T$, so $T = \cos(\omega t + \phi)$; and $c^2X'' = -\omega^2X$ with the boundary conditions, which only certain $\omega_n$ satisfy. The shared constant is the only link. The boundary conditions choose $X_n$, $X_n$ fixes $\omega_n$, and $\omega_n$ sets how fast that shape swells and shrinks. The time factor is a cosine for every instrument in this series, because every equation here is second order in time; everything instrument-specific lives in $X_n$.

</details>
:::

The assumptions were small slopes, tension unchanged by stretching, no bending stiffness and no air. Each later instrument relaxes one of them.

## The recipe for every instrument

Each part repeats two moves. The **operator** is the restoring force per unit mass, written as a function of the shape: tension gives $-c^2\partial_x^2$, bending gives $\kappa^2\partial_x^4$, tension in a sheet gives $-c^2\Delta$. The **boundary conditions** record what each support forbids.

| Support | What it forbids | Condition | Where |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| tied end | moving | $u = 0$ | violin |
| clamp | moving and tilting | $u = 0,\ u' = 0$ | kalimba base |
| free tip | bending moment and shear force | $u'' = 0,\ u''' = 0$ | kalimba tip |
| pin | moving and bending moment | $u = 0,\ u'' = 0$ | piano, idealized |
| rim | moving | $u = 0$ on the circle | drum |
| open end of a pipe | pressure above room pressure | $p = 0$ | clarinet bell, first open hole |
| reed, nearly shut | air moving | $p_x = 0$ | clarinet mouthpiece |

Then the spectrum of the operator fixes the frequencies, and the way the instrument is played fixes how much of each you hear.

```{=html}
<script src="core.js"></script>
<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";
  var C = Core, cv = document.getElementById("beads"), ctx = cv.getContext("2d");
  var N = 5, u = [], v = [], u0 = [], running = false, drag = -1;
  function pluckShape() {
    u = []; v = [];
    for (var j = 1; j <= N; j++) { var x = j / (N + 1), p = 0.25; u.push(x < p ? x / p : (1 - x) / (1 - p)); v.push(0); }
    u0 = u.slice();
  }
  function kOverM() { var s = Math.sin(Math.PI / (2 * (N + 1))); return Math.pow(2 * Math.PI * 0.35 / (2 * s), 2); }
  function F(j, arr) { var a = j > 0 ? arr[j - 1] : 0, b = j < N - 1 ? arr[j + 1] : 0; return a - 2 * arr[j] + b; }
  function geom() { var d = C.fit(cv), W = cv.width, H = cv.height, pad = 22 * d; return { d: d, W: W, H: H, x0: pad, x1: W - pad, mid: H / 2, amp: H * 0.34 }; }
  function bx(g, j) { return g.x0 + (g.x1 - g.x0) * (j + 1) / (N + 1); }
  function draw() {
    var g = geom(), d = g.d; ctx.clearRect(0, 0, g.W, g.H);
    ctx.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--grid"); ctx.lineWidth = d; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(g.x0, g.mid); ctx.lineTo(g.x1, g.mid); ctx.stroke();
    ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb("--ink"); ctx.fillRect(g.x0 - 4 * d, g.mid - 22 * d, 4 * d, 44 * d); ctx.fillRect(g.x1, g.mid - 22 * d, 4 * d, 44 * d);
    ctx.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--muted"); ctx.lineWidth = 1.5 * d; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(g.x0, g.mid);
    for (var j = 0; j < N; j++) ctx.lineTo(bx(g, j), g.mid - g.amp * u[j]);
    ctx.lineTo(g.x1, g.mid); ctx.stroke();
    var sc = (N + 1) / 2;
    for (var j = 0; j < N; j++) {
      var x = bx(g, j), y = g.mid - g.amp * u[j], f = F(j, u) * sc, len = Math.max(-0.9 * g.amp, Math.min(0.9 * g.amp, -f * g.amp * 0.5));
      if (Math.abs(len) > 3 * d) {
        ctx.strokeStyle = C.rgb("--pos"); ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb("--pos"); ctx.lineWidth = 2 * d;
        var y2 = y + len; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x, y); ctx.lineTo(x, y2); ctx.stroke();
        var s = len > 0 ? 1 : -1; ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(x, y2 + s * 6 * d); ctx.lineTo(x - 4 * d, y2); ctx.lineTo(x + 4 * d, y2); ctx.closePath(); ctx.fill();
      }
      ctx.fillStyle = C.rgb(j === drag ? "--accent" : "--ink"); ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, y, Math.max(4, 8 - N / 5) * d, 0, 2 * Math.PI); ctx.fill();
    }
  }
  var last = 0;
  function step(now) {
    if (running && drag < 0) {
      var dt = Math.min(0.05, (now - last) / 1000), sub = 12, h = dt / sub, km = kOverM();
      for (var s = 0; s < sub; s++) { for (var j = 0; j < N; j++) v[j] += h * (km * F(j, u) - 0.12 * v[j]); for (var j = 0; j < N; j++) u[j] += h * v[j]; }
    }
    last = now; draw(); requestAnimationFrame(step);
  }
  function pick(e) {
    var r = cv.getBoundingClientRect(), g = geom(), px = (e.clientX - r.left) * g.d, best = -1, bd = 1e9;
    for (var j = 0; j < N; j++) { var dx = Math.abs(bx(g, j) - px); if (dx < bd) { bd = dx; best = j; } }
    return best;
  }
  function setFromPointer(e) {
    var r = cv.getBoundingClientRect(), g = geom(), py = (e.clientY - r.top) * g.d;
    u[drag] = Math.max(-1.2, Math.min(1.2, (g.mid - py) / g.amp)); v[drag] = 0;
  }
  cv.addEventListener("pointerdown", function (e) { drag = pick(e); running = false; for (var j = 0; j < N; j++) v[j] = 0; cv.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); setFromPointer(e); });
  cv.addEventListener("pointermove", function (e) { if (drag >= 0) { setFromPointer(e); spec(); } });
  cv.addEventListener("pointerup", function () { if (drag >= 0) { drag = -1; u0 = u.slice(); spec(); } });
  document.getElementById("release").addEventListener("click", function () { u0 = u.slice(); running = true; });
  document.getElementById("reset").addEventListener("click", function () { running = false; pluckShape(); spec(); });
  var nb = document.getElementById("nb"), nbo = document.getElementById("nbo");
  nb.addEventListener("input", function () { N = parseInt(nb.value, 10); nbo.textContent = N; running = false; pluckShape(); spec(); });

  function chainParts(shape) {
    var out = [], s1 = Math.sin(Math.PI / (2 * (N + 1)));
    for (var n = 1; n <= N; n++) {
      var a = 0; for (var j = 1; j <= N; j++) a += shape[j - 1] * Math.sin(j * n * Math.PI / (N + 1));
      out.push({ ratio: Math.sin(n * Math.PI / (2 * (N + 1))) / s1, amp: a * Math.sin(n * Math.PI / (N + 1)) });
    }
    return out;
  }
  function spec() {
    var p = chainParts(running ? u0 : u);
    C.stems(document.getElementById("chainSpec"), p, { W: 320, H: 120, rmax: 10, fs: 9, sw: 2.5 });
    var rs = p.slice(0, 5).map(function (q) { return q.ratio.toFixed(3); }).join(", ");
    document.getElementById("chainRead").innerHTML = "N = <b>" + N + "</b> · first ratios <b>" + rs + "</b>";
  }
  document.getElementById("hear").addEventListener("click", function () {
    var p = chainParts(running ? u0 : u).map(function (q) { return { f: 196 * q.ratio, amp: q.amp, tau: 1.3 / (1 + 0.05 * q.ratio * q.ratio) }; });
    C.play(C.render(p, 2.4));
  });
  C.onTheme(function () { spec(); });
  window.addEventListener("resize", draw);
  pluckShape(); spec(); requestAnimationFrame(step);
})();
</script>
```
